sources_quoted.source: data/items.json -> item 3071 "Black Cleaver" -> passives[0] "Carve" -> branches[0] (cached League Wiki text, patch 16.15)
sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 2.3, item 2 ("Black Cleaver average stacks")
sources_quoted.quote: the established model uses a fixed `0.8 * max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +-20% at the extremes. The stack duration (6 s) is always longer than the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic AS*u > 1/6, so expiry does not rescue the constant - this is a documented tuning constant, not a theorem. Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean when a champion module needs exact BC numbers
R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f)

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sources_quoted.quote: Bloodsong 'Expose Weakness' therefore reads 8% (melee holder) / 5% (ranged holder) increased damage taken.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, CLAUDE.md-pinned growth identity, applied to data/champions.json armor rows
sources_quoted.quote: base + growth*(L-1)*(0.7025 + 0.0175*(L-1)); at L=18 the bracket is exactly 1.0, so armor(18) = base + 17*growth. Max base-only armor in the cache is Sejuani 126.65; the modal squishy band is 93-103 (Aphelios/Jinx/Kayle/Seraphine/Sona = 97.4).

scope_limitation.statement: The golden scenario definitions (roster, levels, items, fight window) live under scripts/, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this investigator from reading. The evidence tree (data/ + docs/math-foundations.md) does not contain the 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' tuple - data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json holds 22 unrelated E-series scenarios. An absolute from-scratch recomputation of an outgoing-damage total is therefore not derivable from the permitted sources.
scope_limitation.method_used: Instead of a from-scratch total, I inverted the observed change through the sourced mitigation identity (S3/S4) to recover the item constant the two values encode, and tested that constant against the cached wiki text (S1) and the closed form in S2. This is a decisive test because Carve's constant is bounded above by the wiki (30%) and the feasible band is narrow.

step_2_old_engine_constant.note: 0.8 * 5 stacks * 6% = 24%. S2 identifies this exact constant as the established (pre-change) model and labels it 'a documented tuning constant, not a theorem'.

step_3_exact_closed_form.formula_from_S2: mean stacks = C - C*(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h  (h = number of physical damage instances, h >= 5)
step_3_exact_closed_form.key_fact: The old 24% constant is the exact mean at exactly h = 10 physical damage instances, and understates for every h > 10.

step_4_invert_the_observed_change.identity_used: damage ~ m(R) = 100/(100+R) with R = A*(1 - r) (S3, S4: percentage armor reduction applies to the running armor before penetration)
step_4_invert_the_observed_change.feasibility_floor: A >= 97.54. For any smaller armor the change would require r_new > 30%, which the cached wiki text (S1) forbids. The floor lands exactly on the modal level-18 squishy armor in data/champions.json (Aphelios / Jinx / Kayle / Seraphine / Sona = 97.4), i.e. the new value is reachable, and only just, under the wiki cap.

step_5_verdict_logic.band: Across the entire physically-realizable armor range the change encodes a Carve mean stack count of 4.57 - 5.00 stacks (27.4% - 30.0% armor reduction). The old value encodes exactly 4.00 stacks (24%).
step_5_verdict_logic.why_old_is_wrong: 24% is the S2 closed form evaluated at h = 10 physical damage instances. A coupled roster fight in which breakdown[0] deals >3.2k outgoing damage before death cannot be a 10-hit fight: that would require ~320 post-mitigation damage per instance sustained for the whole window. For every realistic h (roughly 15-40 instances at level 18) the exact Cesaro mean is 26% - 28.5%, strictly above 24%. The old value therefore understates - which is precisely the failure mode S2 predicts and recommends fixing.
step_5_verdict_logic.why_new_is_right: Both self-consistent readings of the new value sit inside the wiki-bounded band and above 24%: (a) against a ~97.5-armor squishy the new value is exactly the wiki cap 30% = 5 stacks (S1), the steady state Carve holds for all but the ramp-in hits given the 6 s stack duration (S2: 'expiry does not rescue the constant'); (b) against a ~200-250 armor target the new value is exactly the S2-recommended Cesaro mean at h = 29-34 instances, which is the self-consistent hit count for that damage total. Under either reading the direction and the magnitude are what the sourced constants require, and the old 24% is the unsourced tuning constant S2 flags.
step_5_verdict_logic.residual_uncertainty: I could not pin the scenario's target armor or hit count from the permitted sources, so I cannot distinguish reading (a) from reading (b). If reading (a) is what the engine now does (a flat 30% cap applied to every hit), it is an upper bound rather than the exact Cesaro mean and overstates by roughly 60/h percentage points of armor reduction (~1-2% of the total at h = 20-30). That residual is an order of magnitude smaller than the old value's error and does not change the sign of the correction, so the verdict stands at new_value_correct rather than both_wrong. Recommended follow-up for a party allowed to read src/: confirm the new BC path implements `C - C*(C-1)/(2h)` (S2's recommendation) rather than a flat cap.

items_ruled_out_as_the_driver.reason: The wiki amp is 8% melee / 5% ranged. A 5% -> 8% correction can move a total by at most +2.857%; the observed move is +3.478%, which no reweighting of that swap can reach. A 0% -> 8% application would need exactly 43.5% of the total to be amped - possible but unmotivated, and it does not reproduce a clean sourced constant, whereas the Black Cleaver inversion lands on 30.000% / 5.000 stacks exactly.
